import FormalConjecturesUtil

/-!
# Erdős Problem 421

*Reference:* [erdosproblems.com/421](https://www.erdosproblems.com/421)
-/

open Set

namespace Erdos421

/--
Is there a sequence $1 \le d_1 < d_2 < \dots$ with density 1 such that all products
$\prod_{u \le i \le v} d_i$ are distinct? -/
@[category research open, AMS 11]
theorem erdos_421 : answer(sorry) ↔
    ∃ (d : ℕ → ℕ), StrictMono d ∧ 1 ≤ d 0 ∧ HasDensity (Set.range d) 1 ∧
    {(u, v) : ℕ × ℕ | u ≤ v}.InjOn fun (u, v) => ∏ i ∈ Finset.Icc u v, d i := by
  sorry

end Erdos421

status_issues.source_status: Solved affirmatively by September 2026. The cited page records an approach sketched by Tao and developed by Chojecki, independent AI-assisted proof claims, and a simplified proof exposition by Kyle Pratt. Pratt’s Theorem 1.1 proves precisely the required existence statement.
status_issues.evidence: The cited page, last edited 1 September 2026 and archived 5 September 2026, explicitly says “The answer is yes” and links https://www.erdosproblems.com/static/421-Pratt.pdf. Theorem 1.1 of that exposition gives a natural-density-one set whose distinct nonempty consecutive blocks have distinct products. The current independent problem catalogue also records #421 as solved.
status_issues.suggested_change: Change the category to `research solved`, replace `answer(sorry)` with `answer(True)`, and cite Pratt’s proof exposition in the documentation. The mathematical right-hand side needs no change.

review.notes: Checked the file’s sole declaration against the cited statement and Pratt’s explicit endpoint-uniqueness formulation. Strict monotonicity and `1 ≤ d 0` enforce positive values; `u ≤ v` excludes empty intervals and includes singletons. `HasDensity` uses real-valued finite counting ratios; its [0,N) convention is equivalent to the source’s [1,N] convention. Scratch proofs verify the meaning of `InjOn`, positivity, density normalization, and rejection of a sequence starting at 1. Computable interval-product tests include collisions and an initial segment of the published greedy sequence. All scratch checks compile without errors or warnings in /workspace/review/scratch.lean. No repository files were edited.
